complexity.correctness_reason: decode and encode recurse once per node, so lists longer than CPython's recursion limit (~1000) raise RecursionError once the 100-node cap is lifted.
complexity.notes: Same approach as before with only the zero fallback respelled as `or`. Per convention the reported time treats the n-digit big-int arithmetic as unit cost, but be aware decode/encode do O(n) big-int operations whose real digit-level work is quadratic. The recursion runs once per node, and ||an iterative pass over both lists carrying the overflow digit|| would avoid both the stack-depth limit and the big integers while staying O(n).
complexity.summary: Recursively decodes both lists into Python integers, adds them, and recursively re-encodes the sum; `encode(a+b) or ListNode(0)` covers the all-zero case since encode(0) returns None.
